- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Religion played a significant role in the social structure of Visigothic society.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Visigoths were initially Arian Christians, while the native Hispano-Romans were largely Catholic Christians.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Visigothic kings used religion to unite their subjects and legitimise their rule.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Failure to adhere to the established religion was considered a political offense and was severely punished.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Visigothic church was a major landowner that controlled vast territories and had significant political power.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The church provided education, healthcare, and charitable services to the populace, particularly the poor.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Priests and bishops wielded significant authority, often acting as judges and arbitrators in local disputes.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Priests and bishops could excommunicate offenders, depriving them of religious and social privileges.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ecclesiastical law governed issues such as marriage and divorce, while secular law dealt with criminal and civil matters.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Church councils were regularly held to establish ecclesiastical law, and the councils' decisions carried considerable weight.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Overall, religion was a unifying force that helped maintain social cohesion and reinforce the ruling authority's legitimacy.
- [USER] User inquired about conflicts between the Visigothic church and the Catholic church and how these were resolved.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There were conflicts between the Visigothic church and the Catholic church.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Visigothic church was initially Arian Christian, while the native Hispano-Romans were largely Catholic Christians.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Catholic church saw the Visigothic church as heretical due to its rejection of the Nicene Creed.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Visigothic kings wished to unify their subjects under a single form of Christianity and gradually converted to Catholicism.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Catholic church invested heavily in missionary work to convert the Visigothic population.
